name: Wilmington
reason: Town wrapper: the flindersandoutback regional page lists it only as a town link, and its draws (Hancock's Lookout, Horrocks Pass) are listed separately as spots; no distinct sight of its own named.

name: Rawnsley Bluff
reason: Named by Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au as a landmark cliff on the Pound's eastern side; a walk or drive to the bluff is a worthwhile stop and a recognisable Flinders feature.

name: Hucks Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names it: lookout over billion-year-old sediments with carpark and picnic area on the Flinders Ranges Way; second-tier guide-named stop.

name: Living with Land Walk
reason: 1 km interpretive stroll to the resort solar farm; minor, one source, near Wilpena resort.

name: Hills Homestead Walk
reason: Wikivoyage: 6.6 km, two-hour return walk to preserved pioneering heritage sites; a named walk.

name: Trezona Hike
reason: Wikivoyage: 8 km, 4-hour hike through the Heysen Range past the Ediacaran Trezona formation; Ediacaran Golden Spike nearby also listed.

name: Boom and Bust Hike
reason: Easy 2 km loop beside the visitor centre; minor, single source, short.

name: Aroona Ruins
reason: flindersandoutback names the scenic Aroona ruins and Aroona Dam kayaking near Leigh Creek as a nature experience; heritage ruins freely visited.

name: Blinman Pools
reason: Tourism board names the hike from Parachilna past scenic ruins to the Blinman Pools; a named walk and swimming oasis.

name: Prairie Hotel
reason: Parachilna's pub is an outback institution named by three flindersandoutback pages (feral food, signature experiences); a recognised landmark rather than an ordinary pub, in the Ohakune Carrot-style roadside-icon class.

name: Southern Flinders Rail Trail
reason: Tourism board names the rail trail as a cycling highlight of the Southern Flinders; a permanent named trail.

name: Caernarvon Track
reason: Listing page and signature-experiences page: the highest 4WD self-drive in the Flinders Ranges, to the 921 m summit of Mount Caernarvon with 360 degree views (The Bunkers Conservation Reserve).

name: Ediacara Conservation Park
reason: For: Wikivoyage names the Ediacara fossil site (Dickinsonia), a world-significant place. Against: the fossil site at Nilpena is reached only through booked station tours, so open public access is doubtful; one counted source.

name: Lake Frome
reason: For: parks.sa.gov.au names the 100 km salt lake as a feature of Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges. Against: ephemeral, edge reached only by 4WD, no named viewpoint or walk; one source.

name: Talc Alf Art Works
reason: Wikivoyage lists the Talc Alf sculpture site in Lyndhurst as its first See item; a quirky outback roadside attraction.

name: Ochre Cliffs
reason: For: Wikivoyage lists the cliffs (Aboriginal ceremonial use, striking colours). Against: 50 km north of Lyndhurst, one source with no access or visit detail.

name: Ochre Pits (Lyndhurst)
reason: Wikivoyage: Ochre Pits on Farina Road 2 km north of Lyndhurst, Aboriginal dreaming significance, with directions; a guide-named roadside stop.

name: Beltana Station
reason: Wikivoyage: Beltana is a historic township where you can easily spend a couple of hours poking about (Afghan camel handlers' water tank, ruins).

name: Pithi Kawi Bush Food Garden
reason: Small town garden in Quorn; only a tourism listing, minor and short visit.

name: Waukarie Falls
reason: For: Parks SA (Mount Brown CP) and the tourism listing name Waukarie Creek, a 5.8 km, 3-hour Heysen Trail walk. Against: the falls run only after rain and the listed experience is a linear walk needing a car shuttle.

name: Remarkable Epic Trail
reason: Mountain-bike trail within Mount Remarkable National Park; part of the larger park listing, one source.

name: Hancock's Lookout
reason: Tourism board singles out Mount Ellen and Hancock's lookouts for views of the Flinders Ranges; a guide-named lookout.

name: Mount Ellen Lookout
reason: Tourism board singles out Mount Ellen and Hancock's lookouts for photographers' views of the Flinders Ranges.

name: Flinders View Park
reason: Wikivoyage lists it with no description; an ordinary town park with no distinct draw.

name: Solomontown Beach
reason: Wikivoyage: a pier, man-made beach and swimming spot with showers and change rooms; second-tier beach stop.

name: Port Pirie National Trust Museum
reason: Tourism board names it among the Southern Flinders heritage highlights; a public museum.

name: Port Pirie Regional Art Gallery
reason: Small regional gallery listed once with no notable collection or draw named; searched the tourism listing only.

name: Port Pirie Mural Trail
reason: Tourism board lists a 2 km, map-guided mural walk through Port Pirie's centre (30+ min to a couple of hours), permanent and open.

name: Port Pirie Heritage Trail
reason: Tourism board lists a self-guided heritage trail of 30+ sites including the Smelter, a named guide walking route; cars or foot.

name: Port Augusta Wharf Precinct
reason: Wikivoyage says the wharf view is hidden behind a supermarket and it is only a recreational precinct; nothing named to see or do for half an hour. Only one source.

name: Blanche Harbor
reason: Wikivoyage names Blanche Harbor as a rehabilitated coastal picnic and birdwatching spot (mulga parrots, emus); second-tier natural stop, open access.

name: Port Augusta Foreshore
reason: Wikivoyage names the foreshore beach with a jetty into deep water, showers and change rooms for swimming; a named beach/jetty stop.

name: Town Carriage Museum (Peterborough)
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Peterborough See listing and the 4-day Southern Flinders itinerary; open railway carriage museum.

name: Glenholme Vineyards (Blesing's Garden)
reason: Cellar door, a business; one itinerary mention only.

name: Wirrabara Silo Art
reason: Itinerary names the Wirrabara silo art as a roadside art icon people stop to photograph; permanent, open. Short stop but a quirky icon.

name: Jarvis Hill Lookout and Walking Trail
reason: Tourism board listing: popular lookout and walking trail near Hawker with views to Wilpena Pound; permanent and free. Dirt road unsuitable when wet.

name: Camel Hump Lookout Walk
reason: Tourism board listing: easy short climb with panoramic views just south of Hawker; named walk, permanent and free.

name: Castle Rock Walk and Lookout
reason: Tourism board listing: castle-shaped rock with a walking track and lookout east of Hawker; named walk, permanent and free.

name: Ferguson Gorge Scenic Drive and Bush Walk
reason: Tourism board listing: scenic drive through Hannigans Gap and 1.6 km walk to a gorge with rock pools and yellow-footed rock-wallabies; 4-5 hours, open to day visitors for a per-vehicle fee (private station land, but access sold to the public).

name: Red Bridge
reason: For: tourism board lists the 1882 Red Bridge on Pekina Creek as a railway landmark with a car park and creek setting. Against: one source, a bridge seen in about 10 minutes, little to do.

name: Fred Teague's Museum
reason: Tourism board lists a compact open museum of minerals, gemstones and fossils at Hawker Motors; indoor visit of 30+ min.

name: Aboriginal Carvings
reason: Tourism board lists Pekina Creek rock carvings as a significant cultural heritage site on a short creek walk from Orroroo's main street; open and free.

name: Adnyamathanha Dreaming Hawker Mural Walking Trail
reason: Tourism board lists a self-guided mural walking tour of Adnyamathanha Dreaming stories with dual-language labels; permanent and open.

name: Buckaringa Sanctuary
reason: AWC sanctuary: AWC's own page gives no visitor arrangements and the Heysen Trail route there has been closed for feral-animal control; no public visit or counted visitor source found (searched AWC, web search, ExplorOz).

name: Horrocks Pass
reason: Wilmington town page and aussietowns name Horrocks Pass with its summit lookout and Horrocks monument, plus Hancocks Lookout views to Spencer Gulf; Heysen Trail passes the monument. Marginal short stop but a guide names it.

name: Kanalla Falls
reason: No counted visitor source found (searched web, Wikipedia only); a waterfall inside Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park, part of the larger park spot, flows only after rain.

name: Mount Serle
reason: No counted source found after searching; a peak on a pastoral station with no visitor page.

name: Mount Hack
reason: No counted source found; the summit lies on the Warraweena property reached only by 4WD track via the station, not a public visit page.

name: Mount Gee
reason: No counted source found after searching; remote peak in the Arkaroola area, not a named visitor stop.

name: Baroota Dam
reason: A water reservoir; no counted visitor source found.

name: Moolawatana Station
reason: A working pastoral station; no counted visitor source and no public visit.

name: Wooltana Station
reason: A working pastoral station; no counted visitor source and no public visit.

name: Willochra Creek
reason: A creek; no counted visitor source naming it as a place to go.
